Liz: ran a focused nsys capture on the 4096-workload yesterday, saw a sharp compile/recompile cluster around 00:12-00:13 of the trace. attaching quick notes.
Sachin: pls paste the nvtx ranges or perfetto link?
Liz: perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace#fake-trace-id (private). NVTX ranges show Batcher:consolidate -> KVShard:reshuffle -> TritonJIT:compile spike.
Arjun: interesting — we usually get warm compiles on first bytes, but reshuffle shouldn't trigger new kernels unless the kernel selector key changed. any hash diffs?
Liz: yes. from nsight timeline I pulled the triton codegen fingerprint header: old_key=(model:v2,seq:64,bs:8,seg:0,ordering:A) new_key=(model:v2,seq:64,bs:8,seg:0,ordering:B). ordering flip caused by KV shard reassign when the batcher coalesced tails.
Kai: ordering B means operator ordering normalized by request arrival instead of model graph order. that's a bug in the batcher canonicalization.
Liz: numbers: before spike compile latency per kernel ~42ms. during spike we saw multiple compiles 380-560ms each, ~72 recompiles in a 2s window. overall 18% p95 token latency bump for that minute.
Sachin: do we have kcache hit/miss counters from Triton or our kernel cache?
Liz: yes. kcache stats in the same run: hits=1204, misses=1834, evictions=412 within 60s slice. Miss ratio jumped from 0.12 -> 0.60 around reshuffle time.
Arjun: sounds like the cache key is sensitive to request-order normalization. two fixes: (1) make key generation order-stable based on static graph metadata, (2) canonicalize batcher output to preserve canonical op order.
Kai: temporary mitigation: treat reshuffle events as debug-only and fall back to previously cached kernels if compile rate exceeds threshold.
PerfBot: Capture summary inserted: nsys=1865009876_4096w.nsys, duration=75s, cuda_compiles=72, avg_compile_ms=312, max_compile_ms=561.
Liz: repro steps I used: 
```
# reproduce locally (fast)
python -m rwi.batcher.test_feed --model redwood/open-v2 --seq-len 64 --clients 40 --reshuffle-prob 0.35 --duration 30
nsys profile -o out --trace=nvtx,cuda python -m rwi.runtime.run_bench --config tmp.json
```
Arjun: Good. Also add a small unit that asserts cache key invariants: sorted(op_names) in key builder. If assert fails, log the operation sequence + request ids.
Sachin: I can add the assert. where does key_builder live? is it runtime/kernel_selector/key_builder.py?
Liz: yes. currently key_builder uses enumerate(ordering_from_batch). change to use model.graph.order or sorted by node name.
Kai: let's prioritize the runtime patch (low risk) + instrumentation to count order-flip frequency. Sachin: can you own the patch? ETA EOD?
Sachin: yes, will cut a PR and include a small perf test. will also add a feature-flag to opt-in for fallback-on-compile-surge.
Liz: after that, we should re-run nsys on CI with reshuffle-prob=0.4 and compare kcache metrics. goal: miss ratio back < 0.2 and compile count < 10 for 60s.
Arjun: add a test that simulates KV shard reassign (unit-level) so this doesn't regress.
Sachin: sounds good. linking my draft branch in thread when ready.
Kai: thumbs up. if we need to roll a hotfix to Dedicated we can ship a build with the fallback feature flag off by default.
Liz: thanks all. I'll collect the perfetto slices & attach a trimmed timeline to the PR.
PerfBot: reminder: tag the PR with perf/regression and add `perf:nsys` label.
Liz: noted.
